$comment: Monsters as data (PLAN §5 'spawn rules as data, not code'). Each is a warning the Anvil shapes in a local costume: the civilization's own material culture blended with the folklore of the ground it surfaces on. For phase 0 that ground is the Toulouse basin, Gascony and the Pyrenees. 'when' is a predicate over the condition vector and cell statics; fields: is_night, phase, moon_illumination, propagation, after_midnight, water_band (0 nearest..3), wild, urban_band (0..3), beacon_grade, poi_density, purity, weather, precip, storm, fog, frost. 'note' is the real-world source and never reaches a player unlabelled; 'fiction' is the Anvil's line (non-negotiable 5).

monsters.name: Hoard-Warden of the Sacred Lake
monsters.note: The Volcae Tectosages of Tolosa sank gold in sacred lakes; Caepio seized it in 106 BCE and it vanished. 'Aurum Tolosanum habet' became the Roman proverb for cursed gain.
monsters.fiction: It counts the ingots still under the water and it knows exactly how many are missing.

monsters.name: Carnyx Howler
monsters.note: The carnyx was a tall bronze war trumpet with a boar's-head bell; seven were found at Tintignac in 2004.
monsters.fiction: A note held so long the boar's head has learned to breathe.

monsters.name: Tantugou of the Fields
monsters.note: Tantugou is the old man of the fields in the folklore of Comminges and Luchon, Haute-Garonne, who guards crops and punishes thieves.
monsters.fiction: It has kept the harvest safe for two thousand years and has finally come to ask who it was keeping it for.

monsters.name: Bécut
monsters.note: The Bécut is the one-eyed giant of Gascon and Béarnais tales, a Pyrenean cousin of the Cyclops who keeps sheep and eats shepherds.
monsters.fiction: One eye, because the other was traded below for a look at the sun.

monsters.name: Matagot
monsters.note: The matagot is the money cat of Gascony and Languedoc: fed first at every meal, it repays the house with a gold coin each morning.
monsters.fiction: It still leaves a coin every morning. Nobody has checked which mint.

monsters.name: Hada of the Spring
monsters.note: The hadas or encantadas are the fairy women of Pyrenean springs and caves, washing linen at dawn and vanishing when watched.
monsters.fiction: The linen it washes has never been dry and was never linen.

monsters.name: Salt-Road Revenant
monsters.note: Hallstatt is named for the Austrian salt mines whose brine preserved Iron Age wool, leather and food; Salies-du-Salat in Comminges worked its own salt spring.
monsters.fiction: Salt kept its cloak, its bread and its grudge.

monsters.name: Cauldron-Thing
monsters.note: Great bronze and silver cauldrons were the feasting and votive vessels of the Iron Age; the Gundestrup cauldron is the best known.
monsters.fiction: Whatever is in it is still warm.

monsters.name: Noria-Wheel Revenant
monsters.note: Cugnaux's norias are chain-and-bucket well wheels, a local heritage trail; several are mapped as ruins.
monsters.fiction: It turns without water, lifting buckets of something else.

monsters.name: Bear-Son of the Pyrenees
monsters.note: Jean de l'Ours, son of a woman and a bear, is the Pyrenean folk hero who carries an iron staff no smith could lift.
monsters.fiction: The staff was forged below, and it wants to know who is still using iron up here.

monsters.name: The Taur
monsters.note: Toulouse's rue du Taur is named for the bull that, in the city's founding legend, dragged Saturninus through the streets in 250 CE.
monsters.fiction: It has forgotten who it was dragging and remembers only the street.

monsters.name: Drac of the Garonne
monsters.note: The drac is the shape-shifting water spirit of Occitan rivers; Toulouse tales place one under the Garonne bridges, luring washerwomen with floating rings.
monsters.fiction: The harbour serpent came up the isthmus with the amphorae and stayed for the river.

monsters.name: Glass-Bead Wraith
monsters.note: Core-formed glass pendant heads with bulging eyes and striped beards were Phoenician trade goods across the Mediterranean, 6th to 3rd century BCE.
monsters.fiction: Every bead is an eye and every eye is keeping count.

monsters.name: Sentinel of the Sign
monsters.note: The sign of Tanit, a triangle under a bar and disc, marks Carthaginian stelae and amulets; grimacing terracotta masks were placed in tombs.
monsters.fiction: It stands where the ground remembers a shrine and it does not care whose.

monsters.name: Amphora-Carrier of the Isthmus
monsters.note: Mediterranean wine and oil reached the Toulouse basin overland from Narbonne along the Aude and Garonne; the oppidum of Vieille-Toulouse is full of imported amphorae.
monsters.fiction: It has carried the same jar since before the road had a name.

monsters.name: Murex Swarm
monsters.note: Tyrian purple was made from the mucus of murex sea snails; thousands of shells went into a single garment, and the middens still mark Phoenician dye works.
monsters.fiction: Ten thousand small mouths, one colour.

monsters.name: Cocagne Shade
monsters.note: Toulouse grew rich in the 15th and 16th centuries on pastel, woad blue, sold as dried balls called cocagnes; the 'pays de Cocagne' is this country.
monsters.fiction: A dyer's shadow, blue to the elbows, mistaking one trade for another.

monsters.name: Charun
monsters.note: Charun, blue-skinned with a hooked nose and a great hammer, guards the door of the tomb in Etruscan painting; the hammer is his, not a weapon he uses on the living.
monsters.fiction: The hammer is for the door. It has been trying a new door.

monsters.name: Vanth
monsters.note: Vanth is the winged female daimon of the Etruscan underworld, carrying a torch and a scroll, a guide rather than a threat.
monsters.fiction: She reads the scroll aloud. Some of the names are still alive.

monsters.name: Tuchulcha
monsters.note: Tuchulcha, with a vulture's beak, donkey's ears and snakes for hair, appears once, in the Tomb of Orcus at Tarquinia.
monsters.fiction: Painted once and never again, because once was enough to be remembered.

monsters.name: Tomb-Fresco Walker
monsters.note: The painted tombs of Tarquinia show dancers, musicians and banqueters in flat profile, red and black on pale plaster.
monsters.fiction: Two-dimensional and aware of it.

monsters.name: Banquet Shade
monsters.note: Etruscan tomb paintings and sarcophagi show couples reclining at the funerary banquet, men and women side by side, which startled Greek visitors.
monsters.fiction: It offers you a cup. The wine is from a vintage that has not happened yet.

monsters.name: Haruspex Echo
monsters.note: Etruscan haruspices read the future in sheep livers; the bronze liver model from Piacenza maps the sky's regions onto the organ.
monsters.fiction: It has read your liver already. It would like a second opinion.

monsters.name: Labyrinth Construct
monsters.note: Placeholder from PLAN §2's bestiary seed.
monsters.fiction: A corridor that walks.

monsters.name: Shabti Swarm
monsters.note: Placeholder from PLAN §2's bestiary seed.
monsters.fiction: Four hundred small servants and no master.

monsters.name: Lamassu Sentinel
monsters.note: Placeholder from PLAN §2's bestiary seed.
monsters.fiction: Five legs, so that it is always both standing and walking.

monsters.name: Golden Stag
monsters.note: Placeholder from PLAN §2's bestiary seed.
monsters.fiction: Its antlers are other animals.

monsters.name: Weight-Golem
monsters.note: Placeholder from PLAN §2's bestiary seed.
monsters.fiction: Exactly one, exactly two, exactly four.

monsters.name: Taotie Devourer
monsters.note: Placeholder from PLAN §2's bestiary seed.
monsters.fiction: A face that is all mouth and no body.

monsters.name: Furnace Spirit
monsters.note: Placeholder from PLAN §2's bestiary seed.
monsters.fiction: Still hot from the first iron.

monsters.name: Were-Jaguar
monsters.note: Placeholder from PLAN §2's bestiary seed.
monsters.fiction: A child's face, a cat's intent.

monsters.name: Lanzón Guardian
monsters.note: Placeholder from PLAN §2's bestiary seed.
monsters.fiction: It smiles with fangs and points both ways.

monsters.name: Reef-Shade
monsters.note: Placeholder from PLAN §2's bestiary seed.
monsters.fiction: Stamped in rows, like the pots.

monsters.name: Earthwork Geometer
monsters.note: Placeholder from PLAN §2's bestiary seed.
monsters.fiction: It measures the ground you stand on and finds it slightly wrong.

monsters.name: Stele-Warden
monsters.note: Placeholder from PLAN §2's bestiary seed.
monsters.fiction: Taller than it should be and carved with doors that open inward.
